findings.title: Deleted selected provider falls back to the default while retaining another provider catalog draft
findings.trigger: Select provider B in a registry containing default custom Responses provider A. Add or edit a manual model catalog for B. Another browser or whole-profile restore removes B. Refresh settings (new epoch/revision) and confirm/apply the retained catalog.
findings.actual: ProviderSettings keeps effectiveId=B and the ModelCatalog key, but its unresolved row falls back to the top-level default-provider summary. That summary has no providerId. ModelCatalog consequently omits providerId from system/models/refresh and accepts the default-shaped receipt. The manager selects the default A for a missing providerId, so the retained B catalog can overwrite A.
findings.consequence: The user can apply capability/model entries to a different provider from the one originally being edited. The original draft-preservation fix must also preserve its target identity.
findings.proof: An isolated .work React + real Api/IndexedDB probe reached an actual system/models/refresh request after B was removed; its params.providerId was undefined. The probe failed exactly at expected providerId=b. Backend selected(current, params.get(providerId)) and public registry shape were read to verify the resulting default-provider route; no live provider was called.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish legacy single-provider payloads from a missing selected connection in a multi-provider registry. Keep the missing target editor/draft under its original identity, show a target-removed warning, and disable all target-bound operations until an explicit valid selection. Require an explicit stable provider identity for the catalog rather than inferring legacy mode from an accidentally absent field. Add removal and profile-replacement regressions while retaining existing late-receipt and draft-preservation safeguards.
findings.relatedEntrypoints: Provider save/remove/default actions currently send explicit effectiveId=B and should be rejected by the backend rather than mutate A; nonetheless gate their misleading missing-target UI consistently. ProviderProfiles resolves selected profile with find and hides actions when absent. ChatGPT login is deliberately shared across instance ChatGPT connections and is not a provider-specific misroute.

method: Whole WEB scope is 253 current source/test/style/entry files. A file list alone was not treated as content review.

Round 2 frontend content coverage came from full2-web, full2-tooling-protocol and this reviewer full2-workspace-web-tests; the only new uncovered files were SettingsDraftDialog and settings-internal-drafts, both freshly read in full. Followed settings draft registry -> pending navigation intent -> nested selectors -> guarded mutation -> compact receipt -> refreshed target. Checked account/session and runtime generations, stale asynchronous completion, explicit recovery and non-replay across these consumers.

Performed one isolated offline adversarial probe in .work, with fixture HTTP responses and no source edits, to establish the cross-provider request defect. No full-suite run or commercial/external MCP call occurred in this audit.

observations: MFA rejection stays local and preserves the known challenge stage; sensitive fields are cleared without treating it as an external authentication redirect. New tests assert the real Api error-shaped contract.
Event tests now construct exact encoded byte sizes, including >2MiB legal ASCII, maximum legal UTF-8 and an oversized multibyte frame followed by reconnection without any mutation replay.

Settings outer and internal navigation guard closures are bound to the active owner and intended destination. Hidden sensitive values/consent are cleared; current providers/model catalog draft target fallback is the exception recorded above.

The conversion modal remains keyed to thread/resource/mode/provider, uses two confirmations, and passes thread/convert as a separate copy request; no current frontend source path mutates the original thread as part of conversion.
The shortened worktree retirement action retains its detailed permanent-retirement warning and exact revision confirmation; its new test checks both wording and submitted identity/revision.
limitations: This is a semantic source/fixture audit plus one offline reproduction, not a new full test matrix. Previously passing tests are not counted again.
